questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 201 asks whether side lengths 3, 4, and 8 can form a triangle. Which answer is correct?

options.text: No because 3 plus 4 is not greater than 8.
Yes because all sides are positive.
No because sides must be equal.

questions.explanation: For a triangle, sum of any two sides must exceed the third. Here 3+4=7, not greater than 8, so no triangle. Positivity alone is insufficient.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 202 has a triangle with base 10 and height 6. What is its area?

options.misconception: uses base times height without half

questions.explanation: Triangle area is one half base times height: 0.5*10*6=30. Forgetting the half or adding dimensions gives wrong values.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 203 shows two triangles with two pairs of equal angles. What similarity criterion applies?

answer.exemplar: The AA similarity criterion applies because two equal angle pairs imply the third angles are also equal, making the triangles similar.

questions.explanation: AA similarity requires only two equal angle pairs; the third follows. Other criteria require side information not given here.
questions.hint: Two equal angles suffice for similarity.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 204 asks which congruence criterion applies when all three sides of one triangle equal all three sides of another. What is the code 1 for SSS?
questions.explanation: SSS congruence applies when all three corresponding sides are equal. The code 1 indicates yes. Other criteria require angle information.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 205 has a right triangle with legs 6 and 8. What is the hypotenuse length?
questions.explanation: By Pythagorean theorem, hypotenuse squared equals 6 squared plus 8 squared equals 100, so hypotenuse is 10. This is a 6-8-10 triangle.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 206 asks for the term for a triangle with all three sides equal. Which term is correct?

options.misconception: confuses no equal sides with all equal
confuses two equal with three equal

questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal. Scalene has none equal, isosceles has at least two, right refers to an angle.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 207 has an equilateral triangle with side 4. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of equilateral triangle with side s is (sqrt3/4)s^2, so for side 4 it is 4*sqrt3. Other formulas miss the height factor.
questions.hint: Use sqrt3 over 4 times side squared.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 208 shows similar triangles with corresponding sides 6 and 9. What is the scale factor from small to large?

answer.exemplar: The scale factor from the smaller triangle to the larger one is 9 divided by 6, which equals 1.5, since corresponding sides are proportional.

questions.explanation: Scale factor is ratio of corresponding sides of image to preimage: 9/6=1.5. Reversing gives 2/3, a different direction.
questions.hint: Divide larger side by smaller side.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 209 asks which criterion applies when two sides and the included angle are equal. What is code 1 for SAS?
questions.explanation: SAS congruence requires two sides and the included angle. The code 1 indicates yes. SSA is not a valid criterion.
questions.hint: Two sides and included angle is SAS.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 210 asks whether 5, 12, 13 is a Pythagorean triple. What is 1 if yes?
questions.explanation: 5 squared plus 12 squared equals 25 plus 144 equals 169 equals 13 squared, so yes. The code 1 indicates a valid triple.
questions.hint: Square and add the two smaller numbers.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 211 has triangle sides 5, 7, and 9. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is sum of side lengths: 5+7+9=21. Multiplying or averaging sides gives wrong values.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 212 has triangle sides 3, 4, 5. What is its area via Heron?
questions.explanation: Semi-perimeter s=6, area sqrt(6*3*2*1)=6. This matches right triangle area 0.5*3*4=6.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 213 shows triangles with side ratios 2:3 and 4:6. Are they similar?

answer.exemplar: The triangles are similar because the side ratios 2:3 and 4:6 simplify to the same proportion 2:3, so corresponding sides are proportional.

questions.explanation: Ratios 2/3 and 4/6 both equal 2/3, so sides are proportional and triangles similar. Unequal ratios would deny similarity.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 214 asks which criterion applies when two angles and the included side are equal. What is code 1 for ASA?
questions.explanation: ASA congruence requires two angles and the included side. The code 1 indicates yes. AAS uses a non-included side.
questions.hint: Two angles and included side is ASA.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute leg from hypotenuse and other leg
questions.stem: Note 215 has a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and one leg 5. What is the other leg?
questions.explanation: Other leg squared equals 13 squared minus 5 squared equals 169-25=144, so leg is 12. This is the 5-12-13 triple.
questions.hint: Subtract square of known leg from hypotenuse squared.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 216 asks for the definition of a median of a triangle. Which description is correct?

options.text: A line parallel to a side.
A segment perpendicular to a side from the opposite vertex.
A segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.explanation: A median connects a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. Altitude, angle bisector, and midsegment are different segments.
questions.hint: Midpoint of opposite side defines median.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 217 has a right triangle with legs 9 and 4. What is its area?

options.misconception: uses product of legs without half

questions.explanation: Area of right triangle is half product of legs: 0.5*9*4=18. Adding or omitting half gives wrong values.

provenance.author: bank-team-geometry
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: Compute missing side in similar triangles
questions.stem: Note 218 shows similar triangles with sides 4 and 6, and 6 and x. What is x?

answer.exemplar: Using proportion 4/6 = 6/x gives 4x = 36, so x = 9. The missing corresponding side is 9 units.

questions.explanation: Proportion 4/6=6/x yields x=9. Cross multiplication avoids ratio reversal errors.
questions.hint: Set up proportion and cross multiply.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 219 asks which criterion applies to right triangles with equal hypotenuse and one leg. What is code 1 for HL?
questions.explanation: HL congruence applies to right triangles with equal hypotenuse and one leg. The code 1 indicates yes.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 220 finds distance between points (0,0) and (3,4). What is the distance?
questions.explanation: Distance formula gives sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5. This is a 3-4-5 right triangle application.
questions.hint: Use Pythagorean theorem on coordinate differences.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 221 asks for the definition of an altitude of a triangle. Which description is correct?

options.text: A segment bisecting the vertex angle.
A segment to the midpoint of the opposite side.
A perpendicular segment from a vertex to the line containing the opposite side.
A segment parallel to the opposite side.

questions.explanation: An altitude is perpendicular from a vertex to the line containing the opposite side. Median, angle bisector, and midsegment differ.
questions.hint: Perpendicular to opposite side defines altitude.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Note 222 has a 30-60-90 triangle with short leg 4. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Short leg 4, long leg 4*sqrt3, area is 0.5*4*4*sqrt3=8*sqrt3. Halving or squaring gives wrong values.
questions.hint: Long leg is short times root 3.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY

answer.exemplar: SSS similarity applies because all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional, which is sufficient to establish similarity.

questions.explanation: SSS similarity requires proportional corresponding sides. AA or SAS similarity require angle information.

answer.exemplar: The area ratio is the square of the scale factor, so 2 squared equals 4. The larger triangle has four times the area.

questions.explanation: Area scales by square of linear scale factor: 2^2=4. Using 2 would be linear, not area.
questions.hint: Square the scale factor for area.

questions.explanation: In a right triangle, hypotenuse is diameter of circumcircle, so radius is half hypotenuse = 5. Using hypotenuse directly gives diameter.

questions.hint: Equal angle plus proportional including sides.

questions.explanation: Long leg 6 means short leg 6/sqrt3 = 2*sqrt3, area is 0.5*2*sqrt3*6 = 6*sqrt3. Other values mishandle the ratio.
